newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan rebels say they seized village in northeast.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say they seized village in northeast.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Friday they had seized a village in northeastern Sudan, killing large numbers of government troops before advancing towards the town of Tokar.

Sampson Kwaje, spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), said rebels overran Marasit, 25 km (15 miles) from Tokar on Thursday and pushed on towards Tokar 150 km (90 miles) southeast of Port Sudan.
"Many enemy troops were killed and we are still counting the bodies," said Kwaje, adding the rebels captured four pickups mounted with anti-aircraft guns and loaded with 100 rockets.
The rebels have said their offensive in the northeast is aimed at cutting the road from Khartoum to Port Sudan on the Red Sea and Sudan's main commercial link with the outside world.
Forces under SPLA leader John Garang's command has stepped up its war this year to topple Khartoum's Islamist government through the rebel National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coalition.
The Sudanese government has accused Eritrean, Ethiopian and Ugandan troops of taking part in rebel offensives in the south, east and northeast. The three countries have denied the charges.
Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it aims to trigger a popular uprising in Khartoum.
